name: Principle of Least Astonishment (POLA)
axiom: A control should do what its appearance and label lead people to expect.
trigger: A familiar control does something unexpected: Save clears the form, a filter reloads the page.

checklist.text: Keep a control's label and function stable across hover, focus, and click; never swap its action.
Preserve typed values when server validation fails and mark the failing fields beside them.
Give destructive actions an undo window or a confirmation that names the object being removed.
Record where users hesitate or backtrack after an action, and treat each as a violated expectation.

antiPattern.violation: Pressing Save Draft clears every field and shows no confirmation, so the draft exists in local storage or nowhere.
antiPattern.remediation: Save Draft shows a saved-at timestamp, keeps the fields filled, and syncs in the background.

parametricParams.caption: THE OUTCOME SHOULD MATCH THE PROMISE

academicOrigin.title: The design of the REXX language
